brief: Decide whether to repair, replace or postpone using stated costs and functional needs.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Replacement Choices"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "¿Reparar, reemplazar o esperar?"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Consertar, trocar ou esperar?"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Decide whether to repair, replace or postpone using stated costs and functional needs.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: The right response depends on safe function, cost and timing; compare the stated options instead of always buying new.
instruction.misconception: The cheapest immediate choice is always right even when it fails required safety, function or timing.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Check safe function and timing first. Then compare repair, replacement and postponement costs under the stated needs and budget.
The stated repair meets the need at lower cost.
No unmet stated need requires immediate replacement.
The replacement meets the stated function, timing and budget constraints.
An unusable or unsafe repair does not meet the need.
Different constraints can make different options appropriate.
The backup makes the lower-cost safe repair feasible.
